headline: Peru Central Bank Increases Foreign Investment Cap for Pension Funds to 51.5%
summary: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru raised the limit for Private Pension Fund Administrators (AFPs) to invest in foreign assets to 51.5%. The decision applies to sovereign and corporate securities outside Peru.
why: Peru's central bank sets regulatory limits on pension fund allocations to manage exchange rate pressures and domestic capital market liquidity.

impacts.name: Peru
impacts.why: Higher foreign investment limits allow institutional funds to reallocate capital internationally.
